findings.title: include_website_name lacks '?' so the untrusted-user restriction is bypassed
findings.body: Active Model Serializers looks for a method named `include_website_name?`, with a question mark. The method here is named `include_website_name`, so it is never called and `website_name` is always serialized. `website_name` is also not listed in `untrusted_attributes`. As a result, TL0 users seen by anonymous visitors expose their website domain and path, even though `website` itself is deliberately hidden for them. Rename the method to `include_website_name?` and apply the same `restrict_user_fields?` check, for example by adding `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain match compares only the suffix, so unrelated domains match
findings.body: When both hosts have the same number of labels (more than two), the code drops the first label of each and compares the rest. With an instance at `forum.co.uk`, a website on `evil.co.uk` would match and show its full path. Likewise `a.example.com` vs `b.example.com` match even though they may be unrelated sites. The heuristic ignores public suffixes and can produce misleading display names.

findings.title: Unparseable website can still raise on later URI parse
findings.body: Only the first `URI(website.to_s)` call is protected by `rescue nil`. The later `URI(website.to_s).path` calls are unprotected, so they re-parse the URL redundantly. The method also mutates the string literal with `"" << website_host`. Parse the URI once and reuse the result, and avoid in-place string mutation.

findings.title: TL0 spec doesn't check website_name is hidden
findings.body: The list of untrusted attributes checked by the TL0 spec does not include `website_name`. The tests therefore miss that the new field leaks for restricted users.
